You are the QA engineer for BackWPup Pro (wp-media/backwpup-pro).

## Config
- REPO: `wp-media/backwpup-pro`
- BASE_BRANCH: `origin/develop`
- CURRENT_MODEL: `Claude Sonnet 4.6`

## Your task

QA review of PR #1687 for issue #1686.

**PR URL:** https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/pull/1687
**PR number:** 1687
**Branch:** `fix/1686-php-deprecated-static-trait-mcp`
**Base branch:** `origin/develop`

### Strategy
**Analysis-only** (Strategy: API / ANALYSIS). This is a backend-only change — a composer patch to a vendor package. No PHP application code in `src/` or `inc/` was modified. No UI elements to test in a browser. Do NOT boot the WordPress environment.

### Acceptance criteria
1. MCP operations (list backups, create backup) no longer produce `PHP Deprecated: Calling static trait method` notices in the error log on PHP 8.1+
2. `composer install` on a clean checkout automatically applies the patch (confirmed by `Applying patches for wordpress/mcp-adapter` in composer output)
3. The patched `vendor/wordpress/mcp-adapter/includes/Transport/Infrastructure/RequestRouter.php` calls `ErrorLogMcpObservabilityHandler::is_sensitive_key()` instead of `McpObservabilityHelperTrait::is_sensitive_key()`

### What to verify (analysis approach)

1. **Read the patch file** at `patches/wordpress/mcp-adapter/fix-static-trait-call.patch` — confirm it targets the right lines and uses `ErrorLogMcpObservabilityHandler` not the trait directly.

2. **Verify the patched vendor file** — check that `vendor/wordpress/mcp-adapter/includes/Transport/Infrastructure/RequestRouter.php` now has the correct call (the patch was applied during backend-agent work).

3. **Verify `ErrorLogMcpObservabilityHandler` exists and uses the trait** — check `vendor/wordpress/mcp-adapter/includes/Infrastructure/Observability/ErrorLogMcpObservabilityHandler.php` to confirm it uses `McpObservabilityHelperTrait` and therefore has `is_sensitive_key()` as a concrete class method.

4. **Verify composer.json** — confirm `cweagans/composer-patches` is in `require`, `allow-plugins`, and `extra.patches` points to the correct patch file.

5. **Check for regression risk** — look at `src/MCP/` to confirm no application code references `McpObservabilityHelperTrait` directly (only the vendor package should).

6. **Post a QA comment** on PR #1687 with your findings using `gh pr comment 1687 --body "..."`.

{"baseRefName":"develop","body":"> [!NOTE]
> ⚠️ AI-generated — created by an automated pipeline. Review before acting on this.

Closes #1686

## Description

Fixes a PHP 8.1+ deprecation notice triggered on every MCP operation (list backups, create backup). The `wordpress/mcp-adapter` v0.5.0 calls `McpObservabilityHelperTrait::is_sensitive_key()` as a static method directly on the trait, which PHP 8.1+ deprecated. This resolves both chained deprecation notices at the root cause.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #(issue number)
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

- `composer install` on a clean checkout: patch applies automatically (`Applying patches for wordpress/mcp-adapter` logged by composer).
- Patched `vendor/wordpress/mcp-adapter/includes/Transport/Infrastructure/RequestRouter.php` verified to call `ErrorLogMcpObservabilityHandler::is_sensitive_key()` instead of `McpObservabilityHelperTrait::is_sensitive_key()`.
- PHPUnit suite: 1287 tests — 2 pre-existing failures (Dropbox API, SaveJobSettings REST) confirmed unrelated to this change (reproduced on baseline).
- `php -l` on the patched file: no syntax errors.

### How to test

1. Check out this branch and run `composer install` — confirm `Applying patches for wordpress/mcp-adapter` appears in output.
2. Trigger an MCP operation (list backups or create backup via an MCP client).
3. Inspect the WordPress error log (`wp-content/debug.log` or equivalent) — no `PHP Deprecated: Calling static trait method` notices should appear.
4. Run `composer test-unit` — no new failures introduced.

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

- MCP feature: backup listing, backup creation, observability/logging sanitisation
- PHP 8.1+ compatibility

## Technical description

### Documentation

The upstream `wordpress/mcp-adapter` v0.5.0 calls `McpObservabilityHelperTrait::is_sensitive_key()` statically on the trait in `RequestRouter::sanitize_params_for_logging()` (line 292). PHP 8.1+ deprecated direct static calls on traits — they must go through a class that uses the trait.

The upstream fix is already merged (WordPress/mcp-adapter PR #193, issue #182), using `ErrorLogMcpObservabilityHandler::is_sensitive_key()` instead. No release with the fix is published yet (`v0.5.0` is latest).

Fix: `cweagans/composer-patches` v1.7 applies a targeted 2-line patch to `RequestRouter.php` on every `composer install`. The patch file mirrors the upstream fix exactly. When upstream ships a fixed release, remove the patch file and the `extra.patches` entry.

### New dependencies

- `cweagans/composer-patches` ^1.7 — Composer plugin to apply patches to vendored packages. Standard ecosystem tool with a strong track record.

### Risks

None. Vendor-layer fix only; no application code in `src/MCP/` changes. Fully reversible once upstream releases a fixed version.

# Mandatory Checklist

## Code validation

- [x] I validated all the Acceptance Criteria. If possible, provide screenshots or videos.
- [x] I triggered all changed lines of code at least once without new errors/warnings/notices.
- [x] I implemented built-in tests to cover the new/changed code.

## Code style

- [x] I wrote a self-explanatory code about what it does.
- [x] I protected entry points against unexpected inputs.
- [x] I did not introduce unnecessary complexity.
- [x] Output messages (errors, notices, logs) are explicit enough for users to understand the issue and are actionnable.

## Unticked items justification

Tests: no new PHPUnit tests needed — the fix is a vendor patch with no application logic change. The patch is verified by running `composer install` and observing the patched file.

## Follow-up tickets

None
